# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 35 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 1 — The Two Angels

**1** "In the first commandment I told you to guard faith, fear, and self-control," he said. "Yes," I agreed. **2** "Now I want to show you the powers behind those virtues — what each one actually is and how they work. **3** Each of them has a double aspect — they apply equally to the righteous and the unrighteous." **4** "Can you explain that, sir?" "Here's the thing," he said. "A righteous person possesses faith and fear and self-control. But living with the righteous person are two angels: one of righteousness and one of wickedness." **5** "But if they both live with me, how do I tell them apart?" **6** "Listen carefully," he said. "The angel of righteousness is gentle, modest, peaceful, sensitive. The moment this angel enters your heart, it begins to speak to you — of righteousness, purity, holiness, contentment, of every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When these things well up in your heart, that's the angel of righteousness at work. **7** Trust him. Trust what he produces. **8** Now, the angel of wickedness — here are his characteristics. He is harsh, angry, and foolish. His work is to pull God's servants down. When he enters your heart, you'll know him by what he brings with him. **9** He stirs up anger, bitterness, stupidity, and every kind of wickedness. When these things rise up in you, that's the angel of wickedness at work. Knowing this, stay as far from him as you can, and never trust anything that comes from him."

---

*PNEUMA note: The Two Angels doctrine gives the believer a practical diagnostic tool — inner states are identified by their source. This is not fatalism; knowing which angel is at work enables the person to resist or respond appropriately.*
